title: Sum-Free Partitions in Finite Abelian Groups and Multiplicative Schur Numbers
contribution_type: Existing archived manuscript with a separately rechecked lower witness

claims.statement: For finite abelian G, S(G,2) = 2 S(G,1) if and only if |G| is odd.
claims.evidence_type: Written theorem in the archived version-2 manuscript.
claims.attribution: Andrei Zabolotskii prompted the observation; Green and Ruzsa supply the one-color formula used in the even-order argument.

claims.statement: S(Z/49Z,2)=32 and S((Z/7Z)^2,2)=28, so general two-color order-invariance is false.
claims.evidence_type: Written corollary of the doubling theorem and Green-Ruzsa formula in the archived manuscript.

claims.statement: MS(3)=16383, under the convention that the colored domain is {2,...,N} and equal factors are allowed.
claims.evidence_type: Archived written upper bound using S(3)=13 and independently replayed complete lower coloring.

assumptions: G is finite abelian. S(G,k) is the maximum size of a subset partitionable into k sum-free sets.
Sum-free excludes x+y=z with x=y allowed; zero cannot occur.
MS(k) excludes monochromatic product triples a,b,ab in {2,...,N}, with a=b allowed.

publication.scope: The existing archive contains the manuscript LaTeX, PDF, and bibliography. It does not contain the complete computational data/software or the newly restored GitHub witness.

events.scope: Version-2 manuscript; not an assertion of the earliest disclosure of every result.

All three public manuscript files matched preserved author files. The MS(3) lower witness was replayed, restored to a public source path, and linked here. This is not a new mathematical result or a new DOI.

review.reproduction: Two enumeration orders checked all 64,449 unordered product triples of the lower witness; a corrupted-color control was rejected. The full S(G,k) solver grid was not replayed.
